FACT_ID: sec16-F01 | anchor: A01
Gasoline-powered vehicles release carbon monoxide through the exhaust pipe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F02 | anchor: A01
Carbon monoxide is deadly and has no detectable smell. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F03 | anchor: A01
Drowsiness inside a vehicle can be a warning of carbon monoxide poisoning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F04 | anchor: A01
The handbook includes fatigue or weakness among carbon monoxide exposure symptoms. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F05 | anchor: A01
Dizziness appears in the handbook's carbon monoxide symptom list. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F06 | anchor: A01
Headache is a listed possible sign of carbon monoxide exposure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F07 | anchor: A01
Nausea or vomiting can indicate carbon monoxide exposure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F08 | anchor: A01
A rapid heart rate is included among the handbook's exposure symptoms. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F09 | anchor: A01
Irregular breathing is included among the handbook's carbon monoxide symptoms. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F10 | anchor: A01
Confusion or disorientation can be a sign of carbon monoxide exposure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F11 | anchor: A01
Coughing is included in the handbook's carbon monoxide exposure warning list. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F12 | anchor: A01
Chest pain is among the handbook's listed exposure symptoms. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F13 | anchor: A01
Inspect and maintain the exhaust system and mufflers regularly to help prevent vehicle carbon monoxide poisoning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F14 | anchor: A01
Have an automotive professional inspect known exhaust holes or other defects immediately. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F15 | anchor: A01
Always turn a keyless vehicle fully off when leaving it in an attached garage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec16-F16 | anchor: A01
On snowy days, inspect the tailpipe and remove blocking snow or ice. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

Misconceptions: absence of odor does not exclude carbon monoxide; a keyless engine can remain running; suspected exposure requires leaving rather than waiting for symptoms to worsen.
Mnemonics: inspect the exhaust, clear the outlet and leave for fresh air if exposure is suspected.
Glossary: carbon monoxide is an odorless exhaust gas; a tailpipe is the exhaust outlet; a detector warns of the gas rather than making the air safe.
